boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain Carnegie Mellon University
boards.description: Late-night dining at CMU is a mix of on-campus staples and nearby Oakland favorites that fuel long study sessions and social breaks.

cards.title: Stack'd Underground
cards.subtitle: Custom Burgers in Morewood Gardens
cards.notes: Located in the lower level of Morewood Gardens, this spot offers smashed burgers and Nashville-style chicken for students staying up late on campus.
cards.short_summary: A student-favorite burger and chicken spot located in the Morewood Gardens residence hall.
cards.evidence_claim: Stack'd Underground operates seven days a week with late-night hours in Morewood Gardens.
cards.source_title: Stack'd Underground Opening in Morewood Gardens - Dining Services
cards.access_notes: Open late during the academic year; check the CMU Dining portal for current daily closing times.

cards.title: Entropy+
cards.subtitle: The Cohon Center Convenience Hub
cards.notes: Grab snacks, sushi, or allergen-friendly meals at this central campus market located on the ground floor of the University Center.
cards.short_summary: The primary on-campus convenience store for late-night snacks and grab-and-go meals.
cards.evidence_claim: Entropy+ is an on-campus convenience store serving snacks and grab-and-go meals in the Cohon Center.
cards.source_title: Entropy+ - Concept - Carnegie Mellon University
cards.access_notes: Standard hours extend into the evening; check the 'What's Open' calendar for late-night availability.

cards.title: The Underground
cards.subtitle: Classic Comfort Food at Morewood
cards.notes: A long-standing campus hangout known for breakfast-all-day, burgers, and famous chicken strips in a relaxed basement setting.
cards.short_summary: A subterranean dining hall in Morewood Gardens offering classic American comfort food.
cards.evidence_claim: The Underground features all-day breakfast and famous chicken strips as a campus favorite hangout.
cards.source_title: the underground - Concept - Carnegie Mellon University
cards.access_notes: Typically open until midnight during the academic semester.

cards.title: Frenchi's Deli & Market
cards.subtitle: South Oakland's Late-Night Legend
cards.notes: Visit Frenchi for a 'Le Pitt Panther' wrap; this corner deli is a staple for students seeking food well past midnight.
cards.short_summary: A beloved local deli in Oakland known for its friendly owner and late-night sandwiches.
cards.evidence_claim: Frenchi's Deli & Market is located in South Oakland and is known for being open late for student eats.
cards.source_title: Frenchi's Deli & Market | Pittsburgh PA
cards.access_notes: Open until 3:00 AM on most nights, making it one of the latest options near campus.

cards.title: Primanti Bros. Oakland
cards.subtitle: The Iconic Pittsburgh Sandwich
cards.notes: Order the classic sandwich topped with fries and coleslaw at this Oakland location, a short walk or bus ride from campus.
cards.short_summary: The Oakland branch of Pittsburgh's most famous sandwich chain, serving late into the night.
cards.evidence_claim: The Oakland location at 3803 Forbes Avenue offers casual dining and is a local staple.
cards.source_title: Oakland - Primanti Bros. Pittsburgh, PA
cards.access_notes: Open until midnight or later; check specific daily hours for late-night kitchen service.

cards.title: Ritter's Diner
cards.subtitle: 24-Hour Breakfast in Shadyside
cards.notes: A classic cash-only diner serving buckwheat pancakes and Greek specialties to the late-night crowd since 1951.
cards.short_summary: A historic 24-hour diner located on the edge of Shadyside, popular for late-night breakfast.
cards.evidence_claim: Ritter's Diner serves breakfast, lunch, and dinner and acts as a late-night snack destination.
cards.source_title: Ritter's Diner: Diner in Pittsburgh, PA
cards.access_notes: Open 24 hours on weekends; verify weekday hours as they may vary. Cash only.

cards.title: Schatz Dining Room
cards.subtitle: All-You-Care-To-Eat in the CUC
cards.notes: The only all-you-care-to-eat hall on campus, Schatz provides a reliable dinner run for students in the Cohon University Center.
cards.short_summary: CMU's primary residential dining hall offering buffet-style meals in the University Center.
cards.evidence_claim: Schatz offers campus's only all-you-care-to-eat dining, serving breakfast, lunch, and dinner.
cards.source_title: Schatz Dining Room - Jared L. Cohon University Center
cards.access_notes: Dinner service typically ends by 9:00 PM, serving as an early late-night option.

cards.title: Rohr Café
cards.subtitle: Italian Coffee in Gates Hillman
cards.notes: Fuel your coding sessions with Italian-style espresso and panini at this cafe located on the 3rd floor of the Gates Hillman Centers.
cards.short_summary: An Italian-style coffee bar by La Prima Espresso located in the computer science building.
cards.evidence_claim: Rohr Café by La Prima serves Italian-style coffee and food on the third floor of Gates Hillman Centers.
cards.source_title: rohr café - la prima - Concept - Carnegie Mellon University
cards.access_notes: Open until 4:00 PM or later during the academic year; check the dining portal for evening hours.

cards.title: Stack'd Oakland
cards.subtitle: Off-Campus Custom Burgers
cards.notes: The off-campus counterpart to the Morewood location, offering a full menu of custom burgers and appetizers late into the night.
cards.short_summary: A popular Oakland burger joint where students can build their own custom meals.
cards.evidence_claim: Stack'd Burgers in Oakland at 3716 Forbes Ave is open late, often until 3:59 AM.
cards.source_title: Stack'd Burgers - Oakland
cards.access_notes: Open until 3:59 AM daily, providing a reliable late-night meal for the Oakland student community.

cards.title: Wean Hall Vending
cards.subtitle: The 24/7 Last Resort
cards.notes: When everything else is closed, the refrigerated vending machines in Wean Hall provide 24/7 access to snacks and beverages for late-night studiers.
cards.short_summary: Reliable 24/7 vending machines located in the high-traffic Wean Hall academic building.
cards.evidence_claim: Refrigerated vending machines in Wean Hall are noted by students as a 24/7 food resource.
cards.source_title: Late Night Food : r/cmu
cards.access_notes: Accessible 24/7 to students with building access.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Discover the functional study hubs, quiet retreats, and collaborative spaces that Carnegie Mellon students use to navigate their rigorous academic schedules.

cards.title: Collaborative Fourth Floor
cards.subtitle: Hunt Library
cards.notes: Utilize the newly renovated collaborative spaces on the fourth floor for group projects and interactive study sessions.
cards.short_summary: A recently updated floor in the main library dedicated to collaborative student work and group study.
cards.evidence_claim: The fourth floor of Hunt Library features a new collaborative study space that can be reserved through the library system.
cards.source_title: Service Updates Fall 2025 - CMU Libraries
cards.access_notes: Open until 3:00 AM most nights during the fall semester.

cards.title: Citadel Teaching Commons
cards.subtitle: Gates and Hillman Centers
cards.notes: Head to this open gathering space for peer-to-peer assistance and collaborative homework sessions in the School of Computer Science.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated collaborative environment for students to work together with peer and TA support.
cards.evidence_claim: The Citadel Teaching Commons in the Gates and Hillman Centers offers a unique environment for students to collaborate with peers and TAs.
cards.source_title: The Citadel Teaching Commons
cards.access_notes: Primarily serves School of Computer Science students but located in a public campus building.

cards.title: Tepper Quad Atrium
cards.subtitle: Tepper Building
cards.notes: Find flexible seating and social interaction zones in this massive, sunlit common area designed for collaboration.
cards.short_summary: A 315,000-square-foot facility featuring a full-height atrium with sweeping staircases and open study areas.
cards.evidence_claim: The Tepper Quad features a full-height atrium with flexible spaces that promote social interaction and collaboration.
cards.source_title: Tepper Quad - Campus Design and Facility Development
cards.access_notes: Includes a fitness center and cafe; open to the campus community.

cards.title: CUC Interview and Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Cohon University Center
cards.notes: Access one of 25 walk-in study rooms equipped with whiteboards for focused individual or small group work.
cards.short_summary: A set of 25 reservable and walk-in rooms in the student union designed for quiet study and interviews.
cards.evidence_claim: The Cohon Center offers 25 interview and study rooms available to all CMU students on a walk-in basis during the semester.
cards.source_title: Interview and Study Rooms - Jared L. Cohon University Center
cards.access_notes: Open until 11:30 PM on Sundays; walk-in only during standard hours.

cards.title: Kraus Campo Rooftop Garden
cards.subtitle: Posner Center
cards.notes: Walk through this meditative rooftop structural garden for a quiet outdoor break between the CFA and Posner Hall.
cards.short_summary: A unique rooftop garden designed by artist Mel Bochner, serving as a meditative outdoor space.
cards.evidence_claim: The Posner Center's rooftop features the Kraus Campo, a meditative outdoor space created by artist Melvin Bochner.
cards.source_title: Posner Center - Environment at CMU
cards.access_notes: Outdoor garden accessible to the public; building interior by appointment or for special collections.

cards.title: The Portal at Sorrells
cards.subtitle: Wean Hall
cards.notes: Visit the fourth floor of Wean Hall to study in 'The Portal,' a specialized area within the engineering and science library.
cards.short_summary: A distinctive study feature within the Roger Sorrells Engineering and Science Library.
cards.evidence_claim: The Portal is a unique feature of Sorrells Library, which is located on the fourth floor of Wean Hall.
cards.source_title: Study in the Portal at Sorrells Library
cards.access_notes: Open until midnight Monday through Thursday during the fall semester.

cards.title: ANSYS Maker Courtyard
cards.subtitle: ANSYS Hall
cards.notes: Observe large-scale student prototypes like solar boats in this outdoor extension of the first-floor maker space.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor courtyard designed for full-size manufacturing and showcasing large student engineering projects.
cards.evidence_claim: ANSYS Hall incorporates a maker assembly space with immediate access to the outdoor Maker Courtyard.
cards.source_title: Ansys Hall - Campus Design and Facility Development
cards.access_notes: The courtyard is a direct extension of the first-floor High Bay Maker Space.

cards.title: Neighborhood Commons
cards.subtitle: Hamerschlag House
cards.notes: Relax by the indoor/outdoor fireplace or use the covered workspace in this newly renovated residential hub.
cards.short_summary: A community space featuring a fireplace, art space, and study areas nestled under Hamerschlag House.
cards.evidence_claim: The Margaret Morrison Street Neighborhood Commons offers a large, covered outdoor workspace with an indoor/outdoor fireplace.
cards.source_title: Margaret Morrison Street Neighborhood Commons
cards.access_notes: Open to all Carnegie Mellon students, faculty, and staff.

cards.title: Mellon Institute Library
cards.subtitle: Mellon Institute
cards.notes: Seek out this quiet, often-empty library for focused study if you have clearance to enter the Mellon Institute.
cards.short_summary: A specialized library known among students for being a quiet and less-crowded study destination.
cards.evidence_claim: The Mellon Institute Library is accessible to Mellon affiliates and is noted by students as a quiet study spot.
cards.source_title: Find a quiet study space in Mellon Institute Library
cards.access_notes: Access is restricted to those with clearance to enter the Mellon Institute building.

cards.title: Newell-Simon Atrium
cards.subtitle: Newell-Simon Hall
cards.notes: Study in the bright, open atrium near the iNoodle cafe, a popular spot for students working in the Robotics Institute.
cards.short_summary: A large, sunlit atrium space frequently used by students for studying and dining.
cards.evidence_claim: Newell-Simon Hall features a great place to study in an atrium located off the main entrance from Forbes Avenue.
cards.source_title: Alternative places to study at CMU
cards.access_notes: Contains the iNoodle dining location; accessible during building hours.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Explore Carnegie Mellon University and its surroundings without spending a dime. From iconic campus traditions and contemporary art to expansive public parks and architectural landmarks, these social activities and spaces are free for students and the public.

cards.title: Contemporary Art Gallery
cards.subtitle: Purnell Center for the Arts
cards.notes: Visit this free public gallery to explore rotating exhibitions of contemporary art focused on societal issues. It is located on the first floor of the Purnell Center.
cards.short_summary: A free contemporary art institute on campus featuring diverse exhibitions and public programs.
cards.evidence_claim: The Miller Institute for Contemporary Art is a free and open public space with no admission fee required for entry.
cards.source_title: Visit - Miller Institute for Contemporary Art - Carnegie Mellon University
cards.access_notes: Open to the public during exhibition cycles; check the official website for current gallery hours.

cards.title: The Campus Message Board
cards.subtitle: The Cut
cards.notes: Gather at this iconic campus landmark to see the latest student messages. Tradition dictates it must be painted between midnight and sunrise to claim it.
cards.short_summary: A central campus landmark used by students as a rotating billboard for announcements and expression.
cards.evidence_claim: The Fence is a student-centered space for free expression and community that has been a CMU tradition for over 100 years.
cards.source_title: The Fence - Student Government - Carnegie Mellon University
cards.access_notes: Accessible 24/7 in the center of campus; painting is governed by student government policies.

cards.title: The Lighted Pedestrian Bridge
cards.subtitle: Connecting Purnell and Gates Centers
cards.notes: Walk across this bridge at night to see the programmable LED light show inspired by 'The Last Lecture.' It links the arts and computer science buildings.
cards.short_summary: A memorial pedestrian bridge featuring a unique LED light installation and symbolic architectural design.
cards.evidence_claim: The Randy Pausch Memorial Bridge features more than 7,000 programmable LED lights with sequences representing themes from Pausch's book.
cards.source_title: Pausch Bridge - Carnegie Mellon University
cards.access_notes: Open 24/7 for pedestrians; the light show typically runs on a loop after dark.

cards.title: Skyward Sculpture
cards.subtitle: Near Warner Hall
cards.notes: View this 100-foot-tall stainless steel sculpture by Jonathan Borofsky. It depicts figures ascending a pole and is a popular campus meeting spot.
cards.short_summary: A towering public art installation on campus representing human potential and ambition.
cards.evidence_claim: Walking to the Sky is an outdoor sculpture by Jonathan Borofsky installed on the CMU campus in front of Warner Hall.
cards.source_title: Walking Art Tour - Carnegie Mellon University | CMU
cards.access_notes: Located outdoors and accessible to the public 24/7.

cards.title: Free Botanical Garden Entry
cards.subtitle: Schenley Park
cards.notes: Show your CMU ID at the admissions desk for free entry to the glasshouse and gardens. It is located just a short walk from the campus edge.
cards.short_summary: A world-class botanical garden offering free admission to enrolled CMU students through the Arts Pass program.
cards.evidence_claim: All graduate and undergraduate CMU students have free access to Phipps Conservatory & Botanical Gardens with their Carnegie Mellon ID.
cards.source_title: Arts Pass - Student Affairs - Carnegie Mellon University
cards.access_notes: Free for students during normal business hours; must present valid CMU student ID.

cards.title: The Band Without Pants
cards.subtitle: Various Campus Locations
cards.notes: Attend free performances by CMU's Scottish-themed marching and concert band. Look for their annual holiday and mid-winter concerts in the University Center.
cards.short_summary: Free public concerts by the university's traditional kilt-wearing band, performing a mix of marches and pop tunes.
cards.evidence_claim: The Kiltie Band performs free concerts, including a holiday concert and two spring concerts, which are open to the campus community.
cards.source_title: The Kiltie Band - Carnegie Mellon University Athletics
cards.access_notes: Concerts are typically held in the Cohon University Center or on the campus quad; check TartanConnect for dates.

cards.title: City Park Exploration
cards.subtitle: Adjacent to Campus
cards.notes: Explore miles of wooded trails, scenic overlooks, and open lawns in this 456-acre park located right next to the university campus.
cards.short_summary: A large regional park bordering campus offering free hiking, running, and recreational spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: Schenley Park, located next door to CMU, offers lots of wooded trails and is a popular spot for outdoor recreation.
cards.source_title: Local Attractions - Dietrich College - Carnegie Mellon University
cards.access_notes: Open daily from 6:00 AM to 11:00 PM; free public access to all trails and lawns.

cards.title: Watch the Buggy Races
cards.subtitle: Schenley Park Course
cards.notes: Join the crowds along Tech Street and Frew Street during Spring Carnival to watch student-built aerodynamic vehicles race at high speeds.
cards.short_summary: A unique CMU tradition where student teams race gravity-powered vehicles through a park course.
cards.evidence_claim: Buggy races are held during Spring Carnival and are free for the public to watch from the sidelines along the course.
cards.source_title: Spring Carnival | Engage with CMU
cards.access_notes: Races occur annually in April; viewing from the public sidewalks along the course is free.

cards.title: Immersive History Walk
cards.subtitle: Hunt Library, 2nd Floor
cards.notes: Step off the elevator to see a digital and physical display of CMU's history, featuring vintage photos, historic posters, and clips of early robots.
cards.short_summary: A curated hallway exhibition in the main library showcasing the diverse history of the university community.
cards.evidence_claim: The University Archives Hallway on the second floor of Hunt Library offers an immersive experience with historic photos and digital screens.
cards.source_title: Resources You Didn't Know the Libraries Had - CMU Libraries
cards.access_notes: Accessible during Hunt Library's regular operating hours; open to students and visitors.

cards.title: The Campus Gateway
cards.subtitle: Forbes Avenue
cards.notes: Relax in the expansive atrium or outdoor plaza of this modern campus hub. It houses the Welcome Center and serves as a central gathering spot.
cards.short_summary: A massive, modern academic and social building with large public atriums and collaborative spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: The Tepper Quad serves as a hub for the campus community and includes the Coulter Welcome Center, which is open to visitors.
cards.source_title: Tepper Quad | Tepper School of Business - Carnegie Mellon University
cards.access_notes: Public areas and the Welcome Center are generally accessible during business hours.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Choose ten distinct study environments. Verify access rules, room or reservation constraints, and the physical affordance that makes each useful. Treat “Claimed by 9am” as editorial framing; never assert crowding or student behavior without evidence.

cards.title: Quiet Study at Hunt Library
cards.subtitle: Dedicated quiet floor in the main campus library
cards.notes: Utilize the third floor for silent individual work. This level is officially designated for quiet study to minimize distractions during intensive research or writing sessions.
cards.short_summary: A designated silent floor within CMU's primary library, ideal for focused individual academic work.
cards.evidence_claim: The third floor of Hunt Library is dedicated to quiet study.
cards.source_title: Is there quiet study space available in the Libraries? - LibAnswers
cards.access_notes: Open to students with a valid CMU ID; specific hours vary by semester and are posted on the library website.

cards.title: Collaborative Tech at Sorrells
cards.subtitle: High-tech study zone in Wean Hall
cards.notes: Visit the fourth floor of Wean Hall to access the Portal, a specialized area featuring technology-equipped group study and project rooms for collaborative engineering and science work.
cards.short_summary: A renovated high-tech collaborative space located on the fourth floor of Wean Hall within the Sorrells Library.
cards.evidence_claim: The Portal is a unique feature of Sorrells Library with technology-equipped group study and project rooms.
cards.source_title: Sorrells Library
cards.access_notes: Group study rooms can be reserved online through the CMU Libraries LibCal system.

cards.title: Private Rooms at the UC
cards.subtitle: Individual and group rooms in the student union
cards.notes: Access one of the 25 interview and study rooms in the Cohon Center. Each room includes a table, chairs, and a whiteboard for private or small group sessions.
cards.short_summary: A collection of 25 versatile rooms in the student union available for individual study or group meetings.
cards.evidence_claim: There are 25 interview and study rooms of different sizes in the Cohon Center featuring chairs, a table, and a whiteboard.
cards.source_title: Interview and Study Rooms - Jared L. Cohon University Center - Student Affairs
cards.access_notes: Rooms are available to all CMU students; check current signage for reservation requirements as they may vary.

cards.title: Open Study at Gates Hillman
cards.subtitle: Modern commons in the computer science complex
cards.notes: Find seating in the third-floor commons or scattered tables on upper floors. The building offers a modern, open environment with natural light and proximity to cafe services.
cards.short_summary: A modern academic complex with various open seating areas and tables suitable for individual or group work.
cards.evidence_claim: The Gates Hillman Center features a large cafeteria area on the 3rd floor and tables scattered throughout the upper floors.
cards.source_title: Gates & Hillman Centers (GHC) - Computing Services
cards.access_notes: Public areas are generally accessible during building hours; some labs and offices require specific department clearance.

cards.title: Collaborative Space at Tepper
cards.subtitle: Expansive commons in the business school
cards.notes: Utilize the open seating and collaborative zones in the Tepper Building. The facility is designed for multidisciplinary interaction with ample desk space and power outlets.
cards.short_summary: A large, modern facility featuring extensive open seating and collaborative spaces for students across all disciplines.
cards.evidence_claim: The Tepper Building includes various technology-enhanced spaces and open commons for student use.
cards.source_title: Tepper Building - Computing Services
cards.access_notes: Open to the campus community; exterior doors may require ID card swipe after hours or on weekends.

cards.title: Historic Study at Mellon Institute
cards.subtitle: Chemistry and science library with classic architecture
cards.notes: Study in a historic setting focused on chemistry and biology literature. This library provides a traditional, quiet atmosphere for serious academic research.
cards.short_summary: A historic library specializing in science literature, offering a quiet and traditional study environment.
cards.evidence_claim: The Mellon Institute Library provides study space and is regarded for its chemistry literature collection.
cards.source_title: Mellon Library
cards.access_notes: Access is restricted to those with clearance to enter the Mellon Institute; check with the library for specific entry requirements.

cards.title: Maker-Adjacent Study at Ansys
cards.subtitle: Modern collaboration zone in the engineering hub
cards.notes: Work in the student collaboration spaces within Ansys Hall. This facility integrates simulation technology and maker spaces with areas for group project development.
cards.short_summary: A 36,000-square-foot facility featuring collaboration spaces and design studios for engineering students.
cards.evidence_claim: Ansys Hall includes student collaboration space, classrooms, and design studios.
cards.source_title: ANSYS Hall - Campus Design and Facility Development
cards.access_notes: Open to all students; connected to Hamerschlag and Porter Halls for easy campus access.

cards.title: Atrium Study at Newell-Simon
cards.subtitle: Bright open space for robotics and CS students
cards.notes: Use the large atrium for open-air study sessions. The space is known for its natural lighting and proximity to the Perlis Atrium, often used for weekend study.
cards.short_summary: A bright, open atrium providing a spacious environment for students to work between classes.
cards.evidence_claim: Newell-Simon Hall features a great place to study in an atrium located off the main entrance.
cards.source_title: Building Access - ID Card Services
cards.access_notes: Standard building access for cardholders; interior doors for specific departments may require additional clearance.

cards.title: Cafe Study at Hunt Library
cards.subtitle: Social study area with coffee service
cards.notes: Combine study with coffee at the Maggie Murph Cafe. The seating area is designed for collaborative work and casual reading in a more social atmosphere than upper library floors.
cards.short_summary: A cafe-based study area within Hunt Library that supports both focused work and collaborative sessions.
cards.evidence_claim: The Maggie Murph Café in Hunt Library supports both focused study and collaborative work.
cards.source_title: Maggie Murph Cafe - Dining Services
cards.access_notes: Accessible during cafe operating hours; seating is open to all library visitors.

cards.title: Special Collections Study
cards.subtitle: Quiet research space for rare materials
cards.notes: Engage with rare books and manuscripts in the newly renovated Posner Center. This space is dedicated to special collections research and discovery in a quiet environment.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated facility for research and engagement with CMU's special collections and rare materials.
cards.evidence_claim: The Posner Center is a dedicated Special Collections library and destination for research.
cards.source_title: The Posner Center for Special Collections
cards.access_notes: Open for research appointments and scheduled visits; check current hours for public access to the gallery and study areas.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Explore the essential corridors and micro-districts surrounding Carnegie Mellon University, from the bustling eateries of South Craig Street to the residential hubs of Squirrel Hill.

cards.title: The Academic Gateway
cards.subtitle: South Craig Street Corridor
cards.notes: Walk this block for independent bookstores and local cafes like EatUnique; it serves as the primary social bridge between CMU and the Carnegie Museums.
cards.short_summary: A vibrant commercial block perpendicular to the Carnegie Museum of Art, popular for student dining and study breaks.
cards.evidence_claim: South Craig Street is a major destination for college students to eat, shop, and relax, located just past the University of Pittsburgh and near CMU.
cards.source_title: South Craig Street Is a Block of Many Wonders - Off the Bluff
cards.access_notes: Public street accessible 24/7; individual business hours vary.

cards.title: The Innovation Corridor
cards.subtitle: Forbes Avenue (Oakland Section)
cards.notes: Navigate the high-tech heart of campus where the Tepper School of Business meets off-campus innovation hubs and quick-service student dining.
cards.short_summary: The main thoroughfare bisecting the campus, lined with university buildings and tech-focused commercial spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: Forbes Avenue is the central corridor for CMU, featuring the Tepper School of Business and numerous dining locations like Scotty's Market.
cards.source_title: DID YOU KNOW? There are several dining locations on CMU's campus to discover!
cards.access_notes: Major public thoroughfare; high pedestrian traffic during class changes.

cards.title: The Graduate Hub
cards.subtitle: Murray Avenue Corridor
cards.notes: Board the 61C bus to reach this district for late-night pizza, grocery runs at Giant Eagle, and a dense concentration of graduate student housing.
cards.short_summary: A primary commercial artery in Squirrel Hill known for its diverse restaurants and essential services for off-campus residents.
cards.evidence_claim: Murray Avenue in Squirrel Hill is a top neighborhood for CMU students, offering shops, restaurants, and easy bus access to campus.
cards.source_title: Neighborhoods of Pittsburgh - Housing & Residential Education
cards.access_notes: Active day and night; well-served by Pittsburgh Regional Transit 61 series buses.

cards.title: The Upscale Escape
cards.subtitle: Walnut Street District
cards.notes: Visit this tree-lined street for boutique shopping and popular cafes; it offers a quieter, more polished atmosphere a short walk from campus.
cards.short_summary: A premier shopping and dining destination in the Shadyside neighborhood, frequently visited by students for weekend outings.
cards.evidence_claim: Shadyside's Walnut Street is a popular area for CMU students, featuring clothing stores and nice restaurants in a walkable setting.
cards.source_title: Off-Campus Housing - Student Affairs - Carnegie Mellon University
cards.access_notes: Pedestrian-friendly commercial block; most shops close by 8:00 PM.

cards.title: The Institutional Link
cards.subtitle: Fifth Avenue Corridor
cards.notes: Observe the grand architecture of Mudge House and the new Fifth and Clyde residence hall along this major transit artery connecting to Downtown.
cards.short_summary: A high-traffic corridor housing several CMU residential buildings and providing direct transit links to the city.
cards.evidence_claim: Fifth Avenue is a main thoroughfare defining the urban site of CMU's Fifth and Clyde Residence and Neighborhood Commons.
cards.source_title: Carnegie Mellon University Fifth and Clyde Residence and Neighborhood Commons
cards.access_notes: Major bus corridor; use designated crosswalks at Morewood Avenue for safety.

cards.title: The Residential Border
cards.subtitle: Beeler Street Corridor
cards.notes: Explore the quiet residential blocks where campus housing meets private rentals; look for the Forbes Beeler Apartments at the corner.
cards.short_summary: A street marking the eastern edge of campus, characterized by a mix of university housing and student-rented houses.
cards.evidence_claim: Beeler Street is a key residential area for CMU students, featuring the Forbes Beeler Apartments at the intersection with Forbes Avenue.
cards.source_title: Forbes Beeler - Campus Design and Facility Development
cards.access_notes: Primarily residential; quiet hours typically observed by neighbors.

cards.title: The Local Favorite
cards.subtitle: Ellsworth Avenue Corridor
cards.notes: Walk this parallel to Walnut Street for a more relaxed vibe, featuring local coffee shops and the historic Admiral apartment building.
cards.short_summary: A Shadyside street known for its independent businesses and popularity among upper-class and graduate students.
cards.evidence_claim: Ellsworth Avenue is a frequently listed location for CMU off-campus housing, featuring properties like The Admiral.
cards.source_title: Off-Campus Housing Marketplace - Carnegie Mellon University
cards.access_notes: Public street; walkable from the north side of campus.

cards.title: The Cultural Crossroads
cards.subtitle: Forbes & Murray Intersection
cards.notes: Head here for the city's best selection of international cuisine and the historic Manor Theatre, just a short bus ride from the UC.
cards.short_summary: The primary commercial intersection of Squirrel Hill, serving as a cultural and dining hub for the CMU community.
cards.evidence_claim: The business districts along Forbes and Murray avenues in Squirrel Hill are active day and night and widely used by students.
cards.source_title: Neighborhoods of Pittsburgh - Housing & Residential Education
cards.access_notes: High-density commercial area; accessible via 61A/B/C/D buses.

cards.title: The East End Connector
cards.subtitle: South Highland Corridor
cards.notes: Explore the border between Shadyside and East Liberty, where modern apartment complexes meet established local eateries.
cards.short_summary: A growing corridor popular for student housing and its proximity to the East Liberty transit center.
cards.evidence_claim: South Highland Avenue is a noted location for student accommodation near CMU, including the Highland Plaza Apartments.
cards.source_title: Highland Plaza Apartments | Student Accommodation
cards.access_notes: Public street; connects the Shadyside and East Liberty business districts.

cards.title: The Greek Way
cards.subtitle: Morewood Avenue Corridor
cards.notes: Walk past the historic mansions housing CMU's fraternity and sorority life, connecting the campus core to the Shadyside neighborhood.
cards.short_summary: A prominent street known for its Greek life housing and as a primary pedestrian route to Shadyside.
cards.evidence_claim: Morewood Avenue is a key campus entrance and corridor for fraternity and sorority life, recently improved with new bike lanes.
cards.source_title: Fifth & Morewood - Campus Design and Facility Development
cards.access_notes: Public street with dedicated bike lanes; heavy pedestrian use near Mudge House.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Discover the unique rituals and long-standing traditions of Carnegie Mellon University, from high-speed buggy races to the world's most painted fence.

cards.title: Painting The Fence
cards.subtitle: A 24-hour vigil for campus expression
cards.notes: Paint the entire structure between midnight and sunrise using only brushes. You must guard it around the clock with at least two people to keep your message from being covered.
cards.short_summary: A central campus landmark on The Cut where students paint messages and maintain 24-hour vigils to protect their work.
cards.evidence_claim: The Fence must be painted between midnight and sunrise, completely covered using only brushes, and guarded by at least two students to remain valid.
cards.source_title: The Fence - Student Government - Carnegie Mellon University
cards.access_notes: Located on The Cut; accessible 24/7 for viewing. Painting is restricted to CMU students.

cards.title: The Buggy Races
cards.subtitle: High-speed aerodynamic engineering
cards.notes: Watch student-built aerodynamic vehicles reach speeds of 35 mph on Schenley Drive. Drivers steer while lying prone inside the carbon-fiber shells.
cards.short_summary: An annual relay race held during Spring Carnival where student organizations compete with custom-engineered gravity-powered vehicles.
cards.evidence_claim: Buggy is a highlight of Spring Carnival where students build and race aerodynamic buggies at speeds up to 35 mph.
cards.source_title: Traditions | Carnegie Mellon University
cards.access_notes: Races occur on Schenley Drive during Spring Carnival. Practice 'rolls' happen on weekend mornings.

cards.title: The Midway Booths
cards.subtitle: Multi-story temporary structures
cards.notes: Explore elaborate, multi-story wooden structures built by student groups in just one week. Each booth features interactive games and decor based on an annual theme.
cards.short_summary: A competitive tradition where student organizations design and build massive, interactive temporary structures on the Midway.
cards.evidence_claim: Student organizations build multi-story structures called booths on the Midway (CFA parking lot) featuring interactive games and decorations.
cards.source_title: Booth - Carnegie Mellon Spring Carnival
cards.access_notes: Booths are open to the public during Spring Carnival weekend in the CFA parking lot.

cards.title: The Mobot Slalom
cards.subtitle: Autonomous navigation challenge
cards.notes: Cheer on autonomous 'mobile robots' as they navigate a wavy white line and pass through gates on the sidewalk. No remote controls allowed.
cards.short_summary: An annual competition where students race autonomous robots along a permanent slalom course painted on the sidewalk.
cards.evidence_claim: Mobot is an annual race where entrants build autonomous robots to navigate a slalom course on the paved walk in front of Wean Hall.
cards.source_title: Mobot - Carnegie Mellon Spring Carnival
cards.access_notes: The race course is permanently painted on the sidewalk in front of Wean Hall.

cards.title: The Bagpipe Degree
cards.subtitle: World's first piping major
cards.notes: Listen for the Pipes and Drums band practicing across campus. CMU was the first university to offer a Bachelor of Fine Arts in Bagpipe Performance.
cards.short_summary: A unique academic program that honors the university's Scottish heritage through professional bagpipe study.
cards.evidence_claim: In 1990, the school instituted the world's first bagpipe degree, a major focusing on studio performance and piping history.
cards.source_title: School of Music - Carnegie Mellon University
cards.access_notes: Performances occur at major university events like Commencement and Carnival.

cards.title: The Band Without Pants
cards.subtitle: Scottish-themed marching ensemble
cards.notes: Spot the marching band wearing traditional kilts during football games. They are known for their irreverent humor and 'scramble' style performances.
cards.short_summary: The university's marching band, famous for wearing kilts and performing entertaining, non-traditional field shows.
cards.evidence_claim: The Kiltie Band began in 1908 and is known for wearing kilts and its 'Band Without Pants' nickname.
cards.source_title: The Kiltie Band - Carnegie Mellon University Athletics
cards.access_notes: Performs at home football games at Gesling Stadium and during Spring Carnival.

cards.title: Scotty the Terrier
cards.subtitle: The whiskered campus icon
cards.notes: Look for the Scottish Terrier mascot at athletic events. The breed was chosen to honor the Scottish roots of founder Andrew Carnegie.
cards.short_summary: The official mascot of CMU, a Scottish Terrier that represents the university's heritage and spirit.
cards.evidence_claim: In 2007, Carnegie Mellon officially welcomed the Scottish Terrier as the university's first mascot, named Scotty.
cards.source_title: Meet Scotty! - Carnegie Mellon University Athletics
cards.access_notes: Appears at various campus events and athletic games.

cards.title: The Skyward Climb
cards.subtitle: A polarizing campus sculpture
cards.notes: Visit this 100-foot-tall stainless steel pole featuring figures 'walking' into the sky. It remains one of the most debated pieces of art on campus.
cards.short_summary: A controversial outdoor sculpture by Jonathan Borofsky that has become a landmark for student discussion and meeting.
cards.evidence_claim: Carnegie Mellon installed Walking to the Sky in May 2006; it depicts figures scaling a 100-foot-tall stainless steel pole.
cards.source_title: Walking to the Sky - News - Carnegie Mellon University
cards.access_notes: Located in front of Warner Hall; accessible to the public 24/7.

cards.title: The 15-Minute Musical
cards.subtitle: Philanthropic performance tradition
cards.notes: Watch fraternities and sororities perform condensed, high-energy versions of popular musicals to raise money for local charities.
cards.short_summary: An annual performance competition where Greek organizations produce short musical theater shows for charity.
cards.evidence_claim: Greek Sing is an annual event where CMU fraternities and sororities perform 15-minute versions of musicals to support local charities.
cards.source_title: Traditions | Carnegie Mellon University
cards.access_notes: Typically held in the spring at a campus theater or outdoor venue.

cards.title: Scotty Saturday
cards.subtitle: A celebration of Tartan pride
cards.notes: Join the campus-wide festival featuring student talent showcases, free snacks, and CMU-themed giveaways to kick off the academic year.
cards.short_summary: A relatively new but established annual tradition that celebrates university spirit and community.
cards.evidence_claim: Scotty Saturday is a daylong celebration of Carnegie Mellon spirit featuring CMU-themed activities and student talent showcases.
cards.source_title: Traditions | Carnegie Mellon University
cards.access_notes: Held annually on campus, usually in the fall.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at Carnegie Mellon University, Shared as Cards
boards.description: Navigate your arrival at CMU with this sequence of essential orientation traditions, campus landmarks, and local Pittsburgh staples accessible with your new student ID.

cards.title: Check In at Welcome Plaza
cards.subtitle: Saturday Afternoon Arrival
cards.notes: Visit the plaza between noon and 4 p.m. to check in, grab your official Class of 2030+ t-shirt, and take your first photos as a Tartan.
cards.short_summary: The primary check-in hub for new students and families during move-in weekend.
cards.evidence_claim: The Welcome Plaza features check-in, photo opportunities, and class t-shirt distribution from noon to 4 p.m. on move-in day.
cards.source_title: Daily Schedule Overview - First-Year Orientation - Carnegie Mellon University
cards.access_notes: Located near the East Campus Garage and Cohon University Center during orientation.

cards.title: Browse the Resource Expo
cards.subtitle: Saturday Afternoon
cards.notes: Meet representatives from campus departments to ask questions about student services and collect useful university literature.
cards.short_summary: An informational fair showcasing campus resources and student support departments.
cards.evidence_claim: The Tartan Resource Expo runs from 2 to 4:30 p.m. on move-in Saturday for new students.
cards.source_title: Daily Schedule Overview - First-Year Orientation - Carnegie Mellon University
cards.access_notes: Typically held in the Cohon University Center or adjacent outdoor spaces.

cards.title: Visit the Most Painted Object
cards.subtitle: Saturday Evening
cards.notes: Walk by this campus landmark on The Cut; it is a student-only bulletin board that must be painted between midnight and sunrise.
cards.short_summary: A central campus landmark and tradition where students paint messages and stand guard.
cards.evidence_claim: The Fence is a long-standing CMU tradition where students paint messages and must guard it to prevent others from repainting.
cards.source_title: A Layered History - CMU125 - Carnegie Mellon University
cards.access_notes: Located in the center of 'The Cut' lawn; accessible 24/7.

cards.title: Attend the President's Welcome
cards.subtitle: Sunday Morning
cards.notes: Join your fellow first-years to hear from the University President as you officially begin your academic journey at CMU.
cards.short_summary: The formal university welcome address for incoming students and their families.
cards.evidence_claim: The President's Welcome is a key orientation event for first-year students and families held on Sunday morning.
cards.source_title: Orientation Schedule - First-Year Orientation - Carnegie Mellon University
cards.access_notes: Location varies by year; check the CMU Events App for the specific venue.

cards.title: Compete in the Carnegie Cup
cards.subtitle: Sunday Afternoon
cards.notes: Participate in this orientation tradition that brings residence halls together for friendly competition and community building.
cards.short_summary: A residence hall-based competition held during the first-year orientation week.
cards.evidence_claim: The Carnegie Cup is an orientation tradition that brings the residence hall communities together.
cards.source_title: First-Year Orientation 2026 - Carnegie Mellon University
cards.access_notes: Events typically held at Gesling Stadium or the East Campus athletic fields.

cards.title: Explore Phipps Conservatory
cards.subtitle: Sunday Afternoon Walk
cards.notes: Use your CMU ID for free admission to these historic glasshouses and botanical gardens located right next to campus.
cards.short_summary: A world-class botanical garden offering free entry to CMU students via the Arts Pass.
cards.evidence_claim: CMU students receive free access to Phipps Conservatory and Botanical Gardens with their university ID.
cards.source_title: Arts Pass - Student Affairs - Carnegie Mellon University
cards.access_notes: Open daily; students must present a valid CMU ID at the admissions desk.

cards.title: Find Your Study Spot
cards.subtitle: Sunday Evening Prep
cards.notes: Visit the university's main library to scout out study spaces; it stays open until 3 a.m. on most nights for late-night sessions.
cards.short_summary: The primary library for arts, humanities, and social sciences at Carnegie Mellon.
cards.evidence_claim: Hunt Library is open until 3 a.m. on Saturdays and Sundays during the academic term.
cards.source_title: Hunt Library - CMU Libraries
cards.access_notes: A valid CMU ID is required to enter the building after 7 p.m.

cards.title: Hike Panther Hollow
cards.subtitle: Monday Morning Refresh
cards.notes: Explore the 456-acre park adjacent to campus; the Panther Hollow trails offer a wooded escape from the city environment.
cards.short_summary: A large urban park bordering campus featuring extensive hiking and running trails.
cards.evidence_claim: Schenley Park is a 456-acre green space popular with CMU students for decompression and outdoor activity.
cards.source_title: Things to do in Pittsburgh - Office of International Education - Carnegie Mellon University
cards.access_notes: Accessible from Frew Street or behind the Phipps Conservatory.

cards.title: Hear the Kiltie Band
cards.subtitle: Monday Evening Tradition
cards.notes: Catch the 'Band Without Pants' at their first rehearsal of the semester at 5:30 p.m. in the CUC Studio Theater.
cards.short_summary: CMU's spirited marching band known for wearing kilts and performing at campus events.
cards.evidence_claim: The Kiltie Band's first rehearsal is typically held on the first day of classes at 5:30 p.m. in the CUC Studio Theater.
cards.source_title: The Kiltie Band - Carnegie Mellon University Athletics
cards.access_notes: Rehearsals are open to the campus community; no audition is required to join.

cards.title: Grab Lunch at Legacy Plaza
cards.subtitle: Monday Lunch Break
cards.notes: Visit the campus food truck for a quick meal; it often features rotating local Pittsburgh restaurants and accepts meal blocks.
cards.short_summary: A student-led food truck program located in Legacy Plaza featuring local cuisine.
cards.evidence_claim: The Tartan Express food truck operates at Legacy Plaza and accepts meal blocks, FLEX, and credit cards.
cards.source_title: Tartan Food Truck Takeover Returns - Dining Services - Carnegie Mellon University
cards.access_notes: Located at Legacy Plaza; hours are typically 10:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m. during the week.
